pull.title: ci: add native freeBSD ci job
pull.body:
This replaces the FreeBSD cross-compilation job with a native build and test job inside a FreeBSD VM. NetBSD and OpenBSD retain their existing cross-compilation jobs.

We currently cross-compile BSD binaries without testing them in this repository. Running tests before merge should help catch platform-specific regressions that would otherwise first appear in nightly builds. This starts with FreeBSD because it has been the most reliable BSD platform in the nightly jobs.

As we don't have native FreeBSD runners, the job uses [vmactions/freebsd-vm](https://github.com/vmactions/freebsd-vm), which is also used by the nightly builds. It reuses the existing CI scripts, depends build, and cache actions where possible.

The VM image is cached after its `prepare` step installs dependencies. The job also restores and saves the usual build caches. Initial testing on free GitHub Actions runners took approximately 60 minutes without caches and 20–30 minutes with caches populated. Performance on Warp runners remains untested.

The VM uses the runner's available CPU count and 75% of its RAM, leaving the remaining memory for the host and VM overhead. There is some overhead after testing while `rsync` copies cache directories back out of the VM.

The patchset also suppresses `lsof` warnings on FreeBSD that would otherwise interfere with functional tests.

Two functional tests are currently excluded:

- `feature_reindex_init` failed during testing.
- `p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1` took an unusually long time.

Both warrant further investigation.

The job requires enabling one additional action:

```text
vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1
```

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

> We currently cross compile various BSD binaries but do not test them. This leads to regressions on master which are noticed in nightly builds and fixed here, recent examples include #36078 and #36145.
> 
> Build **and test** the binaries in this repo as part of our CI instead to avoid this regression/fix flip-flopping.

I think this requires a stronger motivation, to explain that this will actually reduce overall workload.

Those vm-in-a-vm tests are extremely brittle (https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/230#issuecomment-4311704411, https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/issues/81, ... etc)

So if those tasks are added here, we need to understand that this is the "hot path" (for all pull requests) and before this is merged, there needs to be several people who monitor those intermittent failures on those platforms and then categorize them into "intermittent", "unrelated", etc.

If this isn't done, then devs will just ignore all CI results because the false-positive rate is too high and just re-run it until it is green. This may then degrade non-*BSD code at a slight benefit of avoid some trivial test-only BSD fixups.

Maybe I am wrong, but I wanted to raise the point to not miss the large picture here.

> > We currently cross compile various BSD binaries but do not test them. This leads to regressions on master which are noticed in nightly builds and fixed here, recent examples include #36078 and #36145.
> > Build **and test** the binaries in this repo as part of our CI instead to avoid this regression/fix flip-flopping.
>

>

> 
> If this isn't done, then devs will just ignore all CI results because the false-positive rate is too high and just re-run it until it is green. This may then degrade non-*BSD code at a slight benefit of avoid some trivial test-only BSD fixups.
> 
> Maybe I am wrong, but I wanted to raise the point to not miss the large picture here.

We might begin with FreeBSD only, which has shown high stability over a [long period](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/workflows/freebsd.yml?query=event%3Aworkflow_run).

> We might begin with FreeBSD only, which showed a high stability over a [long period](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/workflows/freebsd.yml?query=event%3Aworkflow_run).

Your link shows an unrelated failure for the 35th build (second page). Not sure if this is accurate, but if every 35th build fails and Bitcoin Core has 35 pushes per day, then every day there will be one additional unrelated CI failure.

Maybe there can be a one-month trial period and then a summary is presented with all CI failures and each of them annotated with "intermittent" (y/n), "unrelated" (y/n)? 


Also, even if a failure is related, it can still be intermittent, so merging this pull request does not guarantee to prevent fixups such as https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36145, because the failure happens intermittently.

I did not understand these VMs to be flaky. I didn't observe any flakiness in testing, but probably only ran about 15 runs (x3 jobs), so perhaps I'm due a random flake-failure soon 😋 

The actions _are_ used by a few other high-profile projects like [tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/actions/runs/32341804131/job/96978505535) and [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/actions/runs/33376171138/job/99438039126) as well as:

  - tukaani-project/xz using OpenBSD (workflow)
  - hashcat/hashcat using OpenBSD
  - acmesh-official/acme.sh using OpenBSD
  - aws/aws-lc-rs using FreeBSD (workflow)
  - mozilla/sccache using FreeBSD
  - aristocratos/btop using OpenBSD
  - stalwartlabs/stalwart using FreeBSD
  - deskflow/deskflow using FreeBSD
  - FrameworkComputer/framework-system using FreeBSD
  
But I'd imagine our functional tests put significantly more strain on the vm than any of those projects are doing.
  
I asked codex to take a look at the last months-worth of runs on hebasto's nightly repo:
  
<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

[`hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly`](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly)
from 2026-08-02 through 2026-09-02. Pull-request runs were excluded. The
nightly sample consists of runs with the `workflow_run` event. Manual
`workflow_dispatch` failures are listed separately where they add useful
context.

## Summary

| Workflow | Nightly runs | Successful | Failed | Cancelled |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FreeBSD | 33 | 33 | 0 | 0 |
| NetBSD | 33 | 28 | 4 | 1 |
| OpenBSD | 33 | 10 | 19 | 4 |

The logs for all 29 failed runs were downloaded and inspected.

FreeBSD looks stable in this sample. NetBSD has a small number of nightly
failures, mostly caused by platform resource limits or platform-sensitive
tests. OpenBSD has a high failure rate, but most failures are repeatable test
or platform problems rather than failures to boot the VM.

## NetBSD

### Nightly failures

- [Run 906](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32799434384),
  2026-08-25: `feature_block.py` timed out waiting for the expected peer
  disconnect. Other jobs showed the NetBSD file-descriptor limit.
- [Run 899](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32322734783),
  2026-08-20: `feature_block.py` timed out waiting for a peer disconnect after
  the node had rejected the block.
- [Run 892](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31765546925),
  2026-08-14: `wallet_listtransactions.py` failed when `generateblock`
  returned `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent`.
- [Run 888](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31350308484),
  2026-08-10: `wallet_listtransactions.py` failed with the same
  `TestBlockValidity` error.

The `feature_block.py` failures look like delayed networking or scheduling in
the guest: the node log records the rejection and disconnect, while the test
does not observe the disconnect before its timeout. The wallet failures are
functional test failures and should not be counted as generic VM boot
failures.

### Manual failures

The following manual runs on 2026-08-25 failed during test setup because the
guest did not have enough file descriptors:

- [Run 909](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32837640603)
- [Run 911](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32842679103)
- [Run 912](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32843365189)
- [Run 913](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32852803381)
- [Run 914](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32867589050)

The common messages were:

```text
Not enough file descriptors available. 256 available, 290 required.
Warning: Reducing -maxconnections ... because of system limitations.
```

These are reproducible NetBSD configuration or test-environment failures, not
random VM failures.

There was one additional manual failure:

- [Run 895](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31943115495),
  2026-08-16: the VM boot probe timed out and QEMU was restarted. The run also
  contained `feature_anchors.py` and `interface_http.py` timing failures.

This is the clearest NetBSD example of actual VM or infrastructure flakiness.

## OpenBSD

### Repeated `interface_gui.py` failures

`interface_gui.py` failed in runs [738](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/30731534646),
[739](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/30783225699),
[740](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/30875541319),
[743](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/30972882503),
[744](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31069287625),
[745](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31144016684),
[746](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31234889921),
[747](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31290532291),
[748](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31350308514),
[749](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31452609174),
and [751](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31558633967).

The recurring error was:

```text
GLib-CRITICAL: g_main_context_pop_thread_default:
assertion 'stack != NULL' failed
```

This is highly repeatable across OpenBSD 7.8 and 7.9 GUI jobs. It looks like
an OpenBSD/Qt shutdown or test-environment problem, not QEMU randomly failing.

### Repeated P2P test timeouts

`p2p_private_broadcast.py` or
`p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1.py` failed in runs [738](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/30731534646),
[754](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31765547000),
[757](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31986512649),
[758](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32089854630),
[761](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32322734906),
[765](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32681596291),
[766](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32799434355),
[772](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/33060952442),
and [779](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/33591911980).

The test waited exactly 480 seconds for all addresses to advertise
`NODE_P2P_V2`:

```text
Predicate ... not true after 480.0 seconds
```

The node remained responsive and answered `getnodeaddresses` RPC requests, but
the expected service flags never appeared. Because the same test fails in the
same way across many consecutive OpenBSD runs, this looks like an OpenBSD/test
interaction or severe guest-performance problem rather than a generic boot
failure.

### Package and VM infrastructure failures

- [Run 754](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/31765547000):
  OpenBSD package installation failed with `Premature end of archive` while
  installing `nghttp2`.
- [Run 761](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32322734906),
  [765](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32681596291),
  and [766](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/32799434355):
  package downloads included 404s or connection timeouts.

These failures are package-mirror or network infrastructure failures. They are
separate from the repeated functional test failures.

## Conclusion

For this one-month sample:

- FreeBSD: no observed nightly failures.
- NetBSD: some real guest or scheduling sensitivity, but most failures are
  resource-limit or functional-test issues. The one clear VM boot failure was
  on 2026-08-16.
- OpenBSD: 19 failed nightly runs out of 33. The failure count is dominated by
  repeatable `interface_gui.py` and `p2p_private_broadcast*` failures, with a
  few package-mirror failures. It would be misleading to attribute all 19 to
  vmactions or QEMU flakiness.

The next useful experiment would be to fix or disable the known OpenBSD GUI
and P2P test incompatibilities, raise the NetBSD file-descriptor limit, and
then repeat the same nightly comparison. That would leave a much cleaner
measurement of VM-level reliability.

</details>

I have not observed the interface_gui.py failures that hebasto's repo sees on OpenBSD. I did see a failure on p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1.py once or twice and did have that test disabled on *BSD in one iteration; if that test in particular is flaky it could be disabled on these jobs.

Most of the other failures at first glance appear to be GHA/package archive 404 or other network infra failures and I wouldn't attribute them to the VMs being flaky, so I'm not 100% convinced that critique is warranted.

That said I don't want to add known-flaky jobs and you are correct to call out they could be more work to maintain than porting over a few fixes, if they are unreliable. I suppose the only unclear bit is at what cost level do we prefer to merge buggy code and fix later, vs run more jobs on every PR and merge to prevent that happening in the first place...

> We might begin with FreeBSD only, which has shown high stability over a [long period](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/workflows/freebsd.yml?query=event%3Aworkflow_run).

Happy to start with FreeBSD only if that's preferable.

> > We might begin with FreeBSD only, which has shown high stability over a [long period](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/workflows/freebsd.yml?query=event%3Aworkflow_run).
> 
> Happy to start with FreeBSD only if that's preferable.

Sure, I am not against this pull request, but then the motivation is off, because the two motivating issues are about netbsd and openbsd, which for some reason have a lot more false positive intermittent failures?

It still seems that the remaining fixups required for FreeBSD are less effort than maintaining the FreeBSD ci task here? (Recall that codex only looked at the last month with daily builds, but it missed the failure from 35 days ago and recall that Bitcoin Core has a higher CI volume than just one build per day, so any rare failure will amplify)

Again, seems fine to merge this, but as long as the false positive rate is higher than the true positive rate, it doesn't seem worth it overall.

Scanning the last 90 days (where logs still exist) in hebasto's repo I really only see this one where the vm failed to boot: https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/29139756629/job/86510586228#step:2:188

There are a handful of "random" functional test issues, which could be attributable to the vm-in-vm setup, but I'd recommend [disabling those few tests](https://github.com/willcl-ark/bitcoin/blob/31a2ac55c0dc967b064a2a3e4e91240fb70e7f3c/ci/test/00_setup_env_freebsd_native.sh#L16). There are a number of legitimate functional test failures repeated over many days (e.g interface_gui.py) and few semi-legitimate-looking errors which could have been vm-flakiness.

Including the ~legit test timeout-type failures, but excluding real test failures by my count I see 18 "flaky failures" out of 812 jobs over the 90 days, which or 2.2%.

> as long as the false positive rate is higher than the true positive rate, it doesn't seem worth it overall.

Our CI jobs have between a 7 and 2% fail rate (assuming all current failures are true-positives), per our CI [job statistics](https://willcl-ark.github.io/bitcoin-core-ci-stats/stats/).

So for references 2.2% as a potential false-positive rate is ~ in the same ballpark as the true-failures we see on jobs today (assuming all are true-failures). I agree a flakiness ~= to the bug-catching ability of non-flaky tests isn't great.

If we are more happy to backport fixes from broken nightly/master builds than run CI jobs here as we are worried they'll be too flaky (which is more like a regular CI/CD process to be honest) then that works for me too.

I'll leave this in draft for a few days in case anyone else wants to weigh in, before closing.
Concept ACK on having at least one CI job that runs tests on a *BSD platform.

> Including the ~legit test timeout-type failures, but excluding real test failures by my count I see 18 "flaky failures" out of 812 jobs over the 90 days, which or 2.2%.

Is this the average over all BSDs? Because I see 5 OpenBSD failures in the last 10 days alone, which is more than 10%.

I guess we could add the FreeBSD one only, but I wonder what issues it would have caught this year. Mostly only https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34331?

I'd say we don't care about FreeBSD failures that happen on other platforms as well, so true positive rate is meant as the "marginal" (additional or exclusive) true positive rate.

I guess it could be tried for a month or two, to see what happens in reality.

There is still a flood of unexplained FreeBSD failures:

* https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/43174892437/job/131036635075
* https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/41399624235
* ...

I think those should be fixed first.

Maybe this can be closed in the meantime?

> There is still a flood of unexplained FreeBSD failures:
> 
>    * https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/43174892437/job/131036635075
> 
>    * https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/41399624235
> 
>    * ...
> 
> 
> I think those should be fixed first.

I hope to [collect](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/pull/467) more logs when a failure happens next time.

Sure, logging can't hurt, but I don't think it is possible to fix the OOM or OOS like `System.IO.IOException: No space left on device : '/home/runner/actions-runner/cached/2.338.2/_diag/Worker_20261102-062353-utc.log'`

Isn't that kind of issue a problem with the nightly build infrastructure itself? My recollection is that a lot, if not most, of the issues from that repo have been of a similar nature (timeouts, OOM, out of space, flakiness/can't reproduce) and point to it being under-resourced/unstable, rather than some fundamental problem with these operating systems?
Right, so if this pull is merged, we'll have to deal with a flood of meaningless false reports instead of any real issues that would happen on those systems.

Why? We can pay for (reliable) CPU and enough disk space to be able to properly run tests; and I don't see why anything would be merged if the expectation was it'd just produce pointless noise. 

If anything, it would seem better to have the tests run properly here, than improperly in a different repo, and still have to deal with all the false reports?

Ok, I am not sure if the better hardware will propagate into the double-nested VM (if the inner VM is set up with fixed hard-coded resources), but I guess it seems fine to try and then revert if it doesn't work.
concept ACK, especially with the recent socket stuff the nightly BSD builds as well as individual reviewers are finding things. If we support BSDs I think it would be great to have CI, will review.
Maybe there can be a temp commit on top to spawn a matrix with 100 or 200 tasks for freebsd (or whatever is added) to see if there are any nested vm crashes?
Concept ACK
I mark this as ready for review now, but it will need the `vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1` action approved to be able to run on our CI here.
left some more questions. Also, would be good to push the commit to test this a bunch of times here, before merging into master?
See also #36587, where we are trying to test NetBSD via the macOS CI.

@maflcko I opted to run 20 jobs here as a trial. If they're all successful then I can bump and re-run.

What level of robustness do you think we should aim for here? I calculate that running 200 jobs with 95% confidence would put our failure rate  below ~1.5%. (and 299 runs would put it at 99% reliable).

test: silence lsof warnings on FreeBSD

FreeBSD lsof can emit the following warning during parallel tests:

    lsof: WARNING -- reading lockf list failed: Cannot allocate memory

The functional test runner treats nonempty stderr as failure even when a
test exits successfully.

The lock information is separate from the TCP listener addresses queried
by get_bind_addrs, so suppress lsof warnings for this query while
retaining the tests' socket-address assertions.

NOMERGE: enable cache saves for BSD trials

Allow the BSD robustness trial to populate caches on pull-request runs
and feature-branch pushes so subsequent runs can exercise restoration and
avoid rebuilding dependencies. Retain cache-hit guards and the existing
default-branch save policy for other jobs.

> Why is increasing test coverage here, dependant on filesystem?

`posix_fallocate()` is [disabled](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/commit/96ed2690dfb300033e48384704da6ec45737abee) for ZFS on FreeBSD, so this job exercises a code path that none of the other CI jobs currently tests: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/e211dd0186e9646167d063a16f0da88e5f72e05f/src/util/fs_helpers.cpp#L229-L241
